premises.text: Most historical plastic production becomes waste, yet plastics remain critical to the modern economy
premises.evidence_span: 7.3 billion tons of plastic have been produced since the 1950s, and 86% of that is waste

premises.text: Enzymes can be stabilized and packaged inside plastics so the materials self-degrade when finished
premises.evidence_span: stabilize enzymes and package them up inside of the plastics so they can self-degrade when we're done with them

premises.text: A proprietary coating protects fragile enzymes so they can be embedded and triggered to degrade plastics from the inside
premises.evidence_span: wrap them in our special proprietary coating that acts like PPE and enables us to take these fragile molecules and put them inside the plastics, where they can be triggered to degrade the materials from the inside out

premises.text: Degradation is on demand with water and heat and can run end-to-end to stop microplastics at the source
premises.evidence_span: the degradation is on demand. It requires water and heat. It doesn't happen just on its own

premises.text: Offering is a drop-in additive using small enzyme doses that is readily scalable
premises.evidence_span: We're developing a drop-in additive that's readily scalable. Enzymes are incredibly efficient, so we only need to use a little bit

premises.text: Beachhead is PLA compostable plastics to expand design space and improve end-of-life/regulatory options
premises.evidence_span: We're starting with PLA, which is the first compostable plastic. It's a $3.5 billion market

premises.text: Warm-water or industrial pathways enable decentralized waste processing and chemical recycling
premises.evidence_span: We can also break them down and warm water baths. And this is really important because that simple infrastructure that's easy to scale and maybe gives us a chance to think about decentralizing our waste stream

value.text: Plastics that break down so society can live more harmoniously with nature
value.evidence_span: changing the way that we make and break materials so that we can live more harmoniously with nature

secondary_value.text: Stopping microplastics by degrading polymer chains end-to-end
secondary_value.evidence_span: we stop microplastics at the source

causal_links.evidence_span: 6.3 billion tons of plastic on our land, oceans, air
self-degrade when we're done with them
completely return to the soil at the end of life

notes: Team bios and grant/investor names excluded per §4.2. End-to-end degradation stopping microplastics treated as part of the on-demand degradation mechanism (P4) rather than a second premise. Singleton D1 retained as problem framing that could be revised separately from the enzyme tech.
